# mt76 issue 1179 evidence bundle: 6 GHz HE160 / Apple uplink (XR1710G)

- Upstream issue: <https://github.com/openwrt/mt76/issues/1179>
- Board: Gemtek XR1710G (Airoha AN7581 + MediaTek MT7996)
- Day of capture: 2026-11-14 (device clock UTC; live snapshots 22:17–22:28Z)
- **No device flash, no bootloader/UBI change, no bridge/firewall change** was
  made for this bundle. The 6 GHz experiment added only a temporary UCI BSS,
  reverted with the same `/etc/config/wireless` md5
  (`5f8e7d10fcb16de77eeed815e6bdabf9`) as before it was added.

## What this bundle is, and what it is not

- It is a **5 GHz HE160 2SS baseline plus instrumentation notes** from a board
  that shares the AN7581 + MT7996 platform with the W1700K in the upstream
  report.
- **6 GHz is `not measured (no 6E STA)`.** No 6E-capable station was
  associated with this board in any capture used here, so this bundle claims
  **no 6 GHz throughput, no 6 GHz station dump and no 6 GHz A-MPDU depth**.
- The **Apple uplink falling to 54 Mbit/s is a community report from
  openwrt/mt76#1179, not reproduced here.** No Apple/BCM4388 client was available.
- All numbers below are either read live from the device (`L1`, `L2`), or are
  verbatim excerpts/derived deltas from the earlier 2026-11-14 logs (`P1`–`P3`),
  whose commands are listed in [Provenance](#provenance).

Two provenance caveats that matter for reproducing the `MT76BURST` numbers:

1. The tested image carries a **local, non-upstream instrumentation patch** that
   logs `MT76BURST` from `mt76_txq_send_burst()` every 256 bursts. It is not
   part of this repository branch; treat its numbers as instrumented-build
   values, not as a stock-mt76 behaviour.
2. `MT76BURST` counts **frames handed to the hardware per driver burst**, and
   prints a **cumulative average since module load**. It is not the on-air
   A-MPDU depth (see §3 and §4).

## 2. Repro commands

Copy-paste read-only capture. Run from a host on the same LAN; the AP is
`192.168.1.1` on this test bed.

```sh
ssh root@192.168.1.1

# identity and band layout
date -u
cat /etc/openwrt_release
uname -a
cat /tmp/sysinfo/model
ethtool -i phy0.1-ap0
iw dev
iw reg get
iw phy phy0 info | grep -A2 "Band "

# mt76 debugfs
M=/sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phy0/mt76
cat $M/tx_stats
cat $M/hw-queues
cat $M/token_info

# the burst instrument (instrumented builds only)
dmesg | grep MT76BURST | tail -5

# stations: 5 GHz and 6 GHz
iw dev phy0.1-ap0 station dump
iw dev phy0.2-ap0 station dump

# on-air aggregation counters (per-PPDU MPDU counts; the histogram is broken,
# the counters are usable)
ethtool -S phy0.1-ap0 | grep -E 'ch_time|tx_ampdu|tx_mpdu|rx_ampdu|rx_mpdu'
```

5 GHz HE160 2SS load used for `P1` (device-local source, bypassing the 1 GbE
host feed; the STA was `f8:fe:5e:a1:6f:a8`, 192.168.1.236):

```sh
# on the AP: six local UDP senders, 12 s each
for p in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do /tmp/udpblast 192.168.1.236 9 12 1400 & done

# 1 Hz sampler (the exact lines used by P1):
#   iw dev phy0.1-ap0 station dump | grep -E 'tx bytes|tx packets|tx retries|tx bitrate'
#   cat $M/hw-queues
#   cat $M/token_info
#   cut -d' ' -f1 /proc/uptime
```

`/tmp/udpblast` is a local static aarch64 helper from the earlier measurement
tree (`.research/results/wireless-2026-11-14/tools/udpblast.c`), not part of
this repository. Any equivalent saturated local source works; the absolute
numbers in §5 are only reproducible with the same source/client pair.

## 3. `MT76BURST` excerpts

### 3.1 Earlier 5 GHz HE160 2SS window (`P1`)

The instrumented build recorded a burst average of **27.47 frames/burst** in
the 5 GHz HE160 2SS window: `bursts=7936 frames=218042` (7,936 is an exact
multiple of 256; 218,042 / 7,936 = 27.475). The raw dmesg line was not retained
in the archived log, so this is reported from the measurement record rather
than re-quoted from dmesg:

```text
MT76BURST bursts=7936 frames=218042 avg=27.47      # reported, P1 window
```

This is the number behind the "A-MPDU depth is not 1" statement. It is a
**driver-side** figure: it says the driver handed the hardware ~27 frames per
kick in that window. It does not measure how many MPDUs the firmware put on the
air.

### 3.2 Live boot (`L2`)

The current boot is idle (no STA on either band), and the counter is cumulative
since module load:

```text
$ dmesg | grep MT76BURST | tail -1
[59165.531100] MT76BURST bursts=3786496 frames=15620657 avg=4.12
```

Over the 1,754 retained `MT76BURST` lines the cumulative average reads
`3.91–4.12`; the low value is an idle-tail artefact, not a configuration
change. Do not compare `27.47` with `4.12` unless both windows are rate-matched
and sampled over the same load.

### 3.3 On-air aggregation (same board, `P3`)

The useful on-air indicator is the MIB pair exposed by `ethtool -S`
(`tx_ampdu_cnt` / `tx_mpdu_attempts`), not `MT76BURST`:

| Arm (5 GHz, 1514 B, HE 2SS) | `tx_ampdu_cnt` | `tx_mpdu_attempts` | MPDU/PPDU | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| aggA (4 procs, 10 s) | 951 | 88,666 | **93.2** | `P3` aggA |
| aggB (1 proc, 10 s) | 962 | 122,406 | **127.2** | `P3` aggB |
| aggC (4 procs, 542 B, 8 s) | 949 | 102,752 | **108.3** | `P3` aggC |

Live cumulative values on this boot (idle-dominated) are
`tx_ampdu_cnt=1454776`, `tx_mpdu_attempts=6020188` → 4.14 (`L2`). The
`tx_ampdu_len` histogram in `ethtool -S` is present but reads all zero on this
build, so only the ratio is usable.

## 4. `tx_stats` excerpt and why it is not A-MPDU evidence

Live snapshot (`L2`, 5 GHz band 1; counters are cumulative and were taken while
other lab tests were also running):

```text
Phy phy0, Phy band 1
Length:  1 | 2-10 | 11-19 | ... | 224-247 |
Count:   0 |    0 |     0 | ... |       0 |
BA miss count: 139956
Tx attempts:  6015281 (MPDUs)
Tx success:   5349706 (MPDUs)
Tx PER: 12%
Tx MSDU statistics:
AMSDU pack count of 1 MSDU in TXD:  1801634 ( 56%)
AMSDU pack count of 7 MSDU in TXD:  1092340 ( 34%)
```

6 GHz band 2 in the same read is self-contradictory — zero Tx attempts but
non-zero SU success and A-MSDU counts, while no station is associated and
`ethtool -S phy0.2-ap0` reports `tx_ampdu_cnt=0` / `tx_mpdu_attempts=0`:

```text
Phy phy0, Phy band 2
Tx attempts:        0 (MPDUs)
Tx success:         0 (MPDUs)
Tx PER: 100%
Tx single-user successful MPDU counts: 607635
AMSDU pack count of 7 MSDU in TXD:     638426 ( 25%)
```

In the older `P1` counter read, band 1 had `Tx attempts: 2088358` but only
**560** entries in length bucket 1 and zero in every other bucket (0.027% of
attempts). Conclusion: `tx_stats` length buckets are not usable for A-MPDU
depth on this chip; the upstream capture should use the MIB counters or a
monitor capture.

## 5. `hw-queues` and token excerpts

Live snapshot (`L2`, idle):

```text
PLE page info:
	free pages 0x1ffe, free for all 0x0000, head/tail 0x12d8/0x1b89
	HIF group: max/min quota 0x1da8/0x1da8, used/reserved 0x0000/0x1da8
PLE non-empty queue info:
	BCN Q2: tail/head fid 0x0000/0x0000, packets 1
PSE non-empty queue info:
	SFD PARK Q: tail/head fid 0x03e2/0x03e2, packets 1
```

During the 5 GHz HE160 4/5/6-process window (`P1`), the lowest PLE reading was
`free pages 0x1441` (≈5,185 of 8,192 pages free, ≈36% used); steady-state
samples were mostly `0x1441–0x1457`. `token_count` was mostly `3000–3003 / 16384`
(≈18% in flight) at steady state, with brief dips at process transitions
(`272`, `801`, `1382`). The 6-process arm ended with
`tx retries 1000 / 3,685,265` packets (0.027%). There is no PLE/token
starvation in that window; the limit is not queue memory.

## 7. 5G vs 6G difference

| Property | 5 GHz | 6 GHz |
|---|---|---|
| AP interface | `phy0.1-ap0` (SSID `XR1710G`) | `phy0.2-ap0` (SSID `XR1710G-6G`) |
| Channel / width | ch36, 5180 MHz / 160 MHz, center1 5250 | ch37, 6135 MHz / 320 MHz, center1 6105 |
| Tx power | 23 dBm | 30 dBm |
| Associated station | HE 2SS 160 MHz, -40/-41 dBm, HE-MCS 11 | none (`station dump` empty; 600 s 6G-only BSS idle) |
| `tx_ampdu_cnt` / `tx_mpdu_attempts` (live, cumulative) | 1,454,776 / 6,020,188 | 0 / 0 |
| HE160/320 downlink | **1.224 Gbit/s** netdev-enqueued (f8:fe, 12.50 s); **1.329 Gbit/s** netdev-enqueued (iQOO EHT160, 12.09 s); **1.175 Gbit/s** saturation point by per-STA `aqm` fq enqueue | **not measured (no 6E STA)** |
| A-MPDU evidence | driver burst 27.47 recorded / 3.91–4.12 live cumulative; MIB 93–127 MPDU/PPDU in controlled windows; `tx_stats` histogram unusable | **not measured (no 6E STA)** |

Interpretation:

- The upstream report is 6 GHz **ch85 EHT160 (center idx 79)** with an Apple
  BCM4388 HE 2SS client. This board runs 6 GHz **ch37 EHT320** and has no HE/6E
  client, so the 54 Mbit/s uplink flip cannot be confirmed or refuted here.
- 5 GHz HE160 remains a useful baseline because it exercises the same mt7996
  driver and HE data path; it does not justify carrying any 5 GHz number over
  to 6 GHz (different band, width, txpower and regulatory limits).
- The 1.34 Gbit/s sometimes quoted for the 5 GHz arm is an **enqueue-counter
  upper bound**, not delivered throughput. The retained per-second logs give
  1.224 Gbit/s (f8:fe) and 1.329 Gbit/s (iQOO); the per-STA `aqm` fq-enqueue
  saturation point is 1.175 Gbit/s with an overflowing source. None of these
  are 6 GHz numbers, and none are airtime-completion measurements.

## 8. What we can test next

1. **6 GHz with a real HE/6E client.** Attach an Apple BCM4388 (or another
   HE160 6E) client with the upstream BSS shape — ch85, 160 MHz,
   `he_oper_centr_freq_seg0_idx=79`, `he_bss_color=128`, `he_twt_responder=1`,
   `he_spr_sr_control=3`, `he_6ghz_reg_pwr_type=0` — and capture at association
   and again after the uplink flips to 54 Mbit/s.
2. **Flip detector.** Poll at 1 Hz: `iw dev phy0.2-ap0 station dump` (`rx
   bitrate`), per-STA `agg_status`, and `ethtool -S` deltas
   (`rx_ampdu_cnt`, `rx_mpdu_cnt`, `rx_ampdu_valid_subframe_cnt`,
   `ch_time_rx`); keep the first sample that shows `rx bitrate: 54.0 MBit/s`
   and the following 30 s.
3. **RX-side aggregation.** The symptom is uplink (AP RX), so record the RX BA
   sessions in `agg_status` and the `rx_ampdu_*` MIB before/after the flip;
   verify whether their dialog token/SSN changes (upstream observed unchanged
   sessions).
4. **Same-client 5G vs 6G HE160 A/B**, then repeat with an EHT client as a
   control (upstream reports EHT clients are unaffected).
5. **Instrumentation cleanup.** Prefer the read-only `tx_burst` histogram /
   `non_aql_limit` debugfs over the `MT76BURST` printk, and use the
   `ethtool -S` MIB counters instead of `tx_stats` (read-clear, broken length
   buckets). Never use `iw station dump` `tx bytes` as delivered throughput.
